problem_type: Public onboarding URLs disagree with deployed redirect targets and canonical signals
symptom: OpenSEO finds /handbook and /quickstart as indexable 200 pages while each page declares a .html canonical; the .html sitemap entries return 307 redirects back to the clean URLs.
direct_cause: The deployed site normalizes the onboarding pages to clean URLs, but the marketing content source, page manifest, generated metadata, sitemap, and one static footer still encode .html URLs.
class_root: There is no single enforced invariant that the deployed final URL, rel=canonical, sitemap entry, structured page URL, and internal links for every public onboarding page are identical.
affected_population: Search crawlers clustering duplicate onboarding URLs
Users following homepage, English homepage, or quickstart footer links
Search and analytics reports that split clean and .html URL signals
entry_points: Homepage and English homepage onboarding CTAs
Handbook metadata, structured data, and next-step links
Generated sitemap and SEO contract tests

external_sources.purpose: Google recommends aligning redirects, canonical annotations, and sitemap URLs around one preferred canonical URL.
Google recommends listing the canonical URLs intended for search results in the sitemap.

invariants: Each public onboarding page has one final clean URL used consistently by deployment-facing metadata, structured data, sitemap, and internal links.
Legacy .html URLs remain compatibility redirects only and are not listed as canonical sitemap entries.
The handbook exposes contextual next-step links to relevant Nomi pages and the verified Discussions surface.
generality_proof: The same route constants feed homepage generation, handbook metadata, sitemap rendering, and public tests; the explicit footer scan covers the remaining hand-authored onboarding output. The contract tests assert both positive clean-route usage and negative legacy-route absence across all generated public surfaces.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own the public onboarding destinations consumed by marketing page generation and handbook metadata.
Own the canonical public route set rendered into the sitemap.

shared_boundaries.symbol: public onboarding links use the final clean routes
shared_boundaries.responsibility: Fail delivery when canonical metadata, sitemap-facing pages, or active internal links reintroduce the legacy route form.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Homepage links derive from shared.quickstartUrl and shared.handbookUrl.
The observatory allowlist uses the same clean public routes as the sitemap manifest.

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: Handbook canonical, OG URL, JSON-LD, and next-step links
same_class_entry_points.evidence: Handbook metadata and links derive from shared route constants and are covered by generated-output tests.
This static page contains a hand-authored handbook link and is included in the active output scan.
The repository README uses its own GitHub quick-start anchor and does not publish the marketing onboarding route.

recurrence.reason: A future route rename or hosting normalization can diverge again because generated metadata, manifest, sitemap, and static output have separate consumers.
same_class_scan: Checked content source, site manifest, homepage generator, handbook generator, quickstart footer, generated pages, sitemap, and SEO/static contract tests.
Verified the deployed behavior through the OpenSEO audit: clean routes return 200 and .html routes return 307 to clean routes.

prevention.invariant: All active public onboarding metadata, sitemap entries, and internal links use the same final clean route; legacy .html forms do not appear in those public signals.
prevention.failure_mode: The SEO contract and site static checks fail before delivery when a generated or hand-authored public surface reintroduces .html or drops handbook next-step links.
prevention.strategy: Centralize the route values in the marketing source and manifest, regenerate derived outputs, and assert both the route mapping and class-wide legacy absence.

legacy_paths.rationale: The obsolete .html public URL declarations are removed from active canonical signals; the physical .html files remain as build artifacts and compatibility redirect sources.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The invariant is owned by Nomi's route source, generators, and static tests; no third-party runtime controls the URL decision.

migration: Keep existing .html URLs serving their platform redirect to the clean targets, update first-party links and sitemap immediately, then re-run OpenSEO and Search Console URL Inspection after deployment.
residual_risks: The hosting layer must continue redirecting the old .html paths permanently; repository tests cannot prove the production redirect status.
Search engines may retain old URL clusters temporarily after the signal change; verify the live deployed HTML and URL Inspection rather than relying only on local output.
The clean-route decision is implemented for the current two onboarding pages; any new public page must enter through the same content/manifest contract.
